messages:
jess_support: FYI customer on the line — acme-app reports p99 jump from ~350ms -> ~2.3s starting ~08:17. They see lots of 429s + timeouts. Can someone triage? :phone:

mikko_runtime: looking now. initial check: admission rejects spiked. Grafana shows admit_reject_rate for tenant=acme-app up 18x. Taking logs from runtime.

anya_sre: link please. if it's admission we can either raise tenant burst or route to fallback. but need root cause first.

jess_support: https://grafana.redwood/p/abc123/ingress — p95 panel + per-tenant admit. customer says it started right after a marketing batch. :boom:

mikko_runtime: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-17T08:16:57Z admit_controller.go:123 WARN reject tenant=acme-app reason=concurrency_exceeded active=220 limit=200
2026-03-17T08:17:02Z worker_pool.go:78 INFO queue_depth=480 inflight=190
2026-03-17T08:17:07Z model_exec.go:451 WARN long_tail_ms=1800 tenant=acme-app request_id=xyz
```
Seems a mix of long-tail model execs + tenant hitting concurrency cap -> lots of queued requests getting rejected.

ron_custsuccess: customer confirms they ran 500 parallel users hitting chat-intent API. They have a bursty loop in their retry logic. Will ask them to pause while we mitigate.

mikko_runtime: repro I can run locally: 50 concurrent requests with slightly larger seq length triggers the behaviour. Repro steps:
1) spawn 50 concurrent POSTs to /v1/generate with seq_len=1024 using acme key
2) observe increased per-token time + admit rejects
3) check admin API: `/admin/tenants/acme-app/metrics`

jess_support: any quick mitigations we can do now before we patch?

anya_sre: options: 1) temporarily increase tenant concurrency cap (risk: uses more capacity) 2) apply short TTL routing to fallback quantized model for that tenant 3) enable short client-side backoff note to customer. I vote for 2 + notify.

mikko_runtime: I can flip a routing override for that tenant to `model-text-1.3-quant` which reduces per-token time variance and reduces long-tail. Admin command (will run in 1m):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.redwood/api/tenants/acme-app/override \
  -d '{"route":"model-text-1.3-quant","ttl":"10m"}'
```

eng-oncall: deploy-bot: started rolling the override to serving-plane (canary -> 3 nodes). watch for steady admit_reject_rate.

deploy-bot: rolling override to 3 canary nodes -> success on canary. spreading to pool.

mikko_runtime: override live. admit_reject_rate dropping, p99 back to ~480ms for the tenant, global p99 trending down.

jess_support: told customer to pause their batch and then slowly resume with smaller concurrency and exponential backoff. they acknowledged. :thumbsup:

ron_custsuccess: customer asked for why this happened and an ETA for permanent fix. Suggested follow-ups: improve per-tenant soft-limits + better documentation on retry/backoff.

anya_sre: action items:
- mikko to file runtime change to adjust default concurrency heuristic for long-tail models (PR + perf test)
- platform to add per-tenant temporary auto-fallback policy for detected long-tail spikes (runbook)
- support to provide customer mitigations + recommended retry knobs

mikko_runtime: filing PR now: https://git.redwood/p/r/1029 — will include perf tests and a safety switch. ETA EOD.

jess_support: thanks all. I'll close the loop with the customer and share runbook notes. Marking this as handoff -> Mikko owns follow-up, Anya owns platform runbook.

ron_custsuccess: customer satisfied with temporary fix, will rerun batch with updated backoff this afternoon. keep me posted if anything reappears.

anya_sre: noted. will add automated alert to page eng-oncall if admit_reject_rate > 10/min for a single tenant for >5m.

mikko_runtime: will monitor. tagging this resolved for now, will reopen if the metric flares again. :white_check_mark:
